prompt: Which class does `objects.list` fall in on Cloud Storage's pricing page?
hint: Listing reads names, and the page still does not file it with reading.

choices.text: Class B, with every other request that only reads
choices.why: It only reads, and the page still files it with the writes.

choices.text: Class A, at 0.005 a thousand
choices.why: Right. Listing objects and listing buckets are both Class A.

choices.text: Free, like deleting
choices.why: Deleting is free; listing is not.

choices.text: Billed per GiB of names returned
choices.why: An operation is priced per request, whatever it returns.

prompt: At 0.035 USD per GiB-month and 0.0004 USD per 1,000 Class B operations, how many Class B operations cost the same as storing 1 GiB for a month?
hint: Divide the storage price by the price of one operation.

prompt: Which of these prices on the storage pricing page change when the bucket moves from `us-east1` to `southamerica-east1`?
hint: Look at which tables the page prints per region.

choices.text: Storage, operations and retrieval, since the whole page is regional
choices.why: Only one of the three tables is printed per region.

choices.text: The operation prices, but not the storage
choices.why: It is the other way round.

choices.text: The storage price per GiB-month
choices.why: Right. Operations and retrieval have one table for every single-region bucket.

choices.text: None of them; Cloud Storage has one price everywhere
choices.why: Storage is printed per region: 0.035 in São Paulo.

prompt: A request to read an object comes back 404. What does the pricing page say it costs?
hint: There is a note under the table of classes.

choices.text: A Class B operation, since a read is generally Class B
choices.why: It was a read that failed; the note covers exactly this.

choices.text: Generally nothing; a 4xx is not charged, except a website bucket's 404 page
choices.why: Right. Failed requests are generally free.

choices.text: A Class A operation, the price of an error
choices.why: There is no class for errors.

choices.text: Double, a read plus the error
choices.why: Nothing on the page charges twice for one request.

prompt: Twenty files are copied with one `gcloud storage cp taps/*.json gs://…/`. How many `objects.insert` does the emulator log?
hint: One command, and count the objects.

choices.text: One, since it was one command
choices.why: A command can make many requests; the log counted them.

choices.text: Twenty, one per tap that was sent
choices.why: Right. Each object is its own insert, a Class A each.

choices.text: Forty, one per file and one per check
choices.why: The forty were `getStorageLayout`, not inserts.

choices.text: Two, the packed file and its listing
choices.why: That was the packed run.

prompt: The emulator answered 40 `buckets.getStorageLayout` requests with 404. On a real bucket, what would they be?
hint: The emulator does not implement the method; Cloud Storage does.

choices.text: Answered with 200 and billed as Class B
choices.why: Right. The pricing page lists `getStorageLayout` in Class B.

choices.text: Still 404, since the bucket has no hierarchical namespace
choices.why: The method answers for every bucket; a flat one says it is flat.

choices.text: Free, being a question about the bucket and not about an object
choices.why: Bucket `get`s are Class B like object ones.

choices.text: Class A, because they come before a write
choices.why: The class follows the method, not what comes next.

prompt: A dashboard reads 2,000,000 objects once a day for 30 days at 0.0004 USD per 1,000 Class B operations. How many USD do the reads cost?
hint: Sixty million reads.

prompt: Which of these produce many small objects? Choose all that apply.
hint: The lesson names three sources and one cure.

choices.text: A stream writer flushing whatever arrived in the last few seconds
choices.why: Yes: a file per flush.

choices.text: A prefix per hour per customer
choices.why: Yes: partitions too fine for the data.

choices.text: One object per tap in the app
choices.why: Yes: convenient to write and ruinous to read.

choices.text: A nightly job that joins the day's objects with `objects.compose`
choices.why: That is a cure, not a cause.

prompt: A bucket in `southamerica-east1` serves its first GiB of the month to customers in Brazil. What does the transfer cost?
hint: Check where the free allowance applies.

choices.text: Nothing, the first 100 GB of every month are free
choices.why: The Always Free allowance applies to three US regions only.

choices.text: 0.12 USD, the worldwide price
choices.why: Right. Brazil is in the worldwide band, and the allowance does not reach São Paulo.

choices.text: 0.19 USD, the Premium Tier price for São Paulo
choices.why: That is a virtual machine's table, not the bucket's.

choices.text: 0.035 USD, the storage price
choices.why: Transfer has its own meter.

prompt: Using Cloud Storage's internet tiers (0.12 USD per GiB for the first 10,240 GiB, 0.11 for the next 143,360), what does sending 15,360 GiB in one month cost, in USD?
hint: 10,240 at the first price, the rest at the second.

prompt: Behind Cloud CDN, the `reads.py` line for the images shows requests going UP from 21.47 to 41.34. Why?
hint: Count what every download becomes.

choices.text: The bucket answers more reads, since the cache asks twice
choices.why: The bucket answers fewer: only the misses.

choices.text: Every download is a cache lookup, at 0.0075 per 10,000
choices.why: Right. 53.7 million lookups are 40.27, more than the bucket's own reads cost.

choices.text: Cloud CDN bills its fills as Class A
choices.why: Cache fill is billed per GiB, in the transfer column.

choices.text: The program counts each download twice by mistake
choices.why: It counts the misses once and the lookups once; both are real charges.

prompt: Why is the 1,615.32 of the Cloud CDN line a floor rather than the month's cost?
hint: Something sits between the cache and the bucket.

choices.text: Because cache fill is not counted
choices.why: It is counted: 1 TiB at 0.02, 20.48.

choices.text: Because the external Application Load Balancer that serves the bucket has charges of its own, left out
choices.why: Right. The label says so, and its prices are on the network pricing page.

choices.text: Because Cloud CDN has a minimum monthly fee
choices.why: The CDN page prints no minimum.

choices.text: Because the storage of the images doubles at the edge
choices.why: Cached copies are not billed as Cloud Storage storage.

prompt: A Dataproc cluster in `southamerica-east1-c` reads 3 TiB from a bucket in `southamerica-east1`. What is the transfer charge?
hint: Zones of one region are one location.

choices.text: 0.01 a GiB, for crossing a zone
choices.why: That is between two machines; for a bucket, zones do not count.

choices.text: 0.14 a GiB, from Latin America
choices.why: That is for another region.

choices.text: Nothing; only the operations are billed
choices.why: Right. Same location is free.

choices.text: 0.12 a GiB, as if it went to the internet
choices.why: It never left Google Cloud.

prompt: Private Google ___ lets machines with no external address reach Cloud Storage without going through Cloud NAT, so the 0.045 a GiB of NAT processing disappears.
hint: Two words in the setting's name; the blank is the second.

prompt: A bucket in São Paulo is read by machines in `southamerica-west1` (Santiago) and in `us-central1` (Iowa). How do the two transfer prices compare?
hint: Read the Latin America row of the matrix.

choices.text: Santiago is cheaper, being on the same continent
choices.why: A North American bucket gets that discount; a Latin American one does not.

choices.text: Iowa is cheaper, being where Google's network is densest
choices.why: Every cell of the row is the same.

choices.text: Both are 0.14 a GiB
choices.why: Right. Every destination from a Latin American bucket costs 0.14.

choices.text: Both are free, being inside Google Cloud
choices.why: Only the same location is free.

prompt: On a Requester Pays bucket, which charge stays with the bucket's owner?
hint: One meter is about keeping, not using.

choices.text: The operations
choices.why: The requester pays for those.

choices.text: The network transfer
choices.why: The requester pays for that too.

choices.text: Storage, the keeping of the data
choices.why: Right. The owner keeps paying to keep the data; reading it moves to the reader.

choices.text: Nothing: every line moves to the requester
choices.why: Storage, and early deletion, stay with the owner.

prompt: `gcloud storage cat --billing-project=planner-dev …` sent no `X-Goog-User-Project` header in this lab. What explains it?
hint: Look at what the lab told `gcloud` about credentials.

choices.text: The emulator strips the header before logging
choices.why: The count was taken from `gcloud`'s own `--log-http`, before the emulator.

choices.text: `gcloud` adds that header beside the credentials, and this lab sends none
choices.why: Right. `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_DISABLE_CREDENTIALS` turns both off.

choices.text: `--billing-project` is ignored by `gcloud storage`
choices.why: It is a flag every `gcloud` command takes.

choices.text: The bucket was not Requester Pays, so `gcloud` saw no need
choices.why: `gcloud` sends it whatever the bucket's setting.

prompt: Quitanda's taps cost 34.57 a month, almost all requests. Which change cuts the most?
hint: Look at what the requests are counting.

choices.text: Moving the taps to Nearline, which stores for less
choices.why: Nearline's operations cost more, and there is a retrieval fee on every read.

choices.text: Writing them as 64 MiB files, or composing them nightly
choices.why: Right. 123 objects instead of 2 million: 0.27 a month.

choices.text: Reading them with the Python client instead of `gcloud`
choices.why: Each object is still one read, whatever the client.

choices.text: Putting Cloud CDN in front of the bucket
choices.why: The dashboard is inside Google Cloud; a cache for viewers does not help it.
